claim.quote: An excess over known backgrounds is observed at low energies and most prominent between 2 and 3 keV.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date. Published as Phys. Rev. D 102, 072004 (2020).

key_value_text.quote: the excess favors a monoenergetic peak at (2.3+-0.2) keV (68% C.L.) with a 3.0 sigma global (4.0 sigma local) significance
key_value_text.value: Excess most prominent between 2 and 3 keV; if interpreted as a monoenergetic peak, centered at (2.3 ± 0.2) keV (68% C.L.) with 3.0σ global (4.0σ local) significance; the abstract does not claim a discovery.

name: Excess Electronic Recoil Events in XENON1T
notes: This is explicitly not a discovery, observation or confirmed dark-matter signal: the abstract reports 'An excess over known backgrounds' and treats each explanation (axion, neutrino magnetic moment, tritium, bosonic dark matter) as a hypothesis, with a trace of tritium that can 'neither be confirmed nor excluded'.

Later XENONnT electronic-recoil analysis (https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.11330): "we observe no excess above background"; its abstract also gives a background about 5 times lower than in XENON1T ("(15.8 ± 1.3) events/(tonne×year×keV), the lowest ever achieved in a dark matter detector and ~5 times lower than in XENON1T").

significance.quote: The solar axion model has a 3.4 sigma significance ... The significances of the solar axion and neutrino magnetic moment hypotheses are reduced to 2.0 sigma and 0.9 sigma, respectively, if an unconstrained tritium component is included in the fitting.
significance.value: up to 3.4σ (solar axion hypothesis, before an unconstrained tritium component is included in the fit; 2.0σ with it)

summary.plain: In 2020 XENON1T reported an excess of low-energy electron-recoil events over known backgrounds, most prominent at 2–3 keV. The paper tested solar-axion, neutrino-magnetic-moment, tritium and bosonic-dark-matter explanations (3.0σ global to 3.4σ) and says a trace of tritium can neither be confirmed nor excluded. A later XENONnT analysis with lower background reports no excess.
summary.technical: XENON1T low-energy electronic-recoil search, 0.65 t-y exposure, background rate 76 ± 2 events/(t y keV) between 1 and 30 keV. An excess over known backgrounds is observed, most prominent between 2 and 3 keV. Solar axion 3.4σ, enhanced neutrino magnetic moment 3.2σ, tritium β decay 3.2σ (the first two fall to 2.0σ and 0.9σ if an unconstrained tritium component is included in the fit); for bosonic dark matter the excess favors a monoenergetic peak at (2.3 ± 0.2) keV with 3.0σ global (4.0σ local) significance. The abstract reports an excess over known backgrounds; it does not claim a discovery.

title: Excess Electronic Recoil Events in XENON1T
why_it_matters: The abstract reports an excess over known backgrounds and weighs three explanations (solar axions, an enhanced neutrino magnetic moment, tritium); it says the axion and neutrino-magnetic-moment results are in strong tension with stellar constraints and that a trace of tritium can neither be confirmed nor excluded. The later XENONnT electronic-recoil analysis, with a background about five times lower, reports no excess above background.
